audit.title: Policy Library

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Opens with a self-contained definition: "ACE ships with a library of pre-built, audited policies… Each policy is a standalone smart contract that plugs into a PolicyEngine." Each table row is independently liftable.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; measured 1 H1, 1 table, 0 level skips, 0 sections over 600 words. The table is the correct structure for this content. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured 3 numerals, 0 with units, and vague quantifier "most." Descriptions are qualitative ("a minimum or above a maximum") where a parameter name or type would help.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Adequate. 16 internal links (every policy + the composition concept page), but 0 external/primary. Named entities like Proof of Reserve and Keystone Forwarder are unlinked.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Each row is a verbatim-liftable claim, e.g. BypassPolicy "immediately allows the transaction and skips all remaining policies."

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, datePublished/dateModified absent from head. A visible "Last Updated: 2026-07-17" exists in body but is not machine-exposed.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Not applicable in substance (0 code blocks); appropriate for an index page, scored neutral rather than penalized.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Adequate. Covers the "what is available" query but lacks symptom-/goal-phrased entry points ("which policy enforces a rate limit," "how do I allowlist senders").

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent PascalCase policy naming aids entity resolution. No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a clean reference-index page for the ACE policy library: a one-paragraph definition plus a 14-row table mapping each policy to a crisp one-line description. Its biggest GEO strength is a well-structured, highly liftable table with consistent terminology — an ideal RAG chunk. Its biggest opportunity is machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical, no head dates) and intent-phrased coverage: the page answers "what policies exist" but not "which policy do I use for X" the way developers and agents actually query. Honest verdict: a solid, agent-friendly index that is under-served by missing schema and use-case-oriented entry points.

recommendations.title: Add a "when to use" / use-case column or lead phrase
recommendations.issue: Rows describe *behavior*, not *intent* — "Rejects the transaction if the extracted value exceeds a configured maximum."
recommendations.change: Add a third column ("Use when…") or a leading clause per row, e.g. MaxPolicy → "Cap a per-transaction amount." VolumeRatePolicy → "Enforce a rolling rate limit per account." This mirrors how devs/agents query by goal.
recommendations.why: Intent-phrased text wins retrieval for "which ACE policy for rate limiting / allowlisting" that behavior-only prose loses.

recommendations.title: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD and canonical URL
recommendations.issue: Measured 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, dateModified absent from head.
recommendations.change: Add JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified: 2026-07-17`, `inLanguage`, and a canonical `<link>` to the non-`.md` URL. Surface the existing body "Last Updated" date as `dateModified`.
recommendations.why: Structured freshness + canonical raise agent parseability and E-E-A-T trust; the date already exists in prose but is invisible to parsers.

recommendations.title: Link named external entities to their canonical pages
recommendations.issue: "Checks a Chainlink Proof of Reserve feed" and "Keystone Forwarder" are named but unlinked (0 external/primary links measured).
recommendations.change: Link "Proof of Reserve" and "Keystone Forwarder" to their canonical Chainlink docs pages.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative links raise citation rate and let engines resolve the referenced products.

recommendations.title: Replace the vague quantifier and add one concrete count
recommendations.issue: "cover the most common compliance and access control patterns."
recommendations.change: State the count: "ACE ships with 14 pre-built, audited policies covering access control, volume/rate limits, identity, and reserve checks."
recommendations.why: A concrete count is a high-lift, verbatim-liftable specific; "most common" is a vague qualifier engines discount.

recommendations.title: Group the table by category
recommendations.issue: 14 flat rows with no grouping; category is only inferable.
recommendations.change: Add category sub-headers or a category column (Access Control, Value/Volume, Identity, Reserves, Lifecycle). Preserves the single table while adding a scannable axis.
recommendations.why: Explicit categorization lets engines build justified "which type of policy" answers.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifier "most common" in the intro (flagged in measured facts) — see P3.
No keyword stuffing, marketing fluff, or unresolved cross-references. Entity naming is consistent.
offPageNotes: The body references `/llms.txt`; confirm this page is enumerated there so agents discover it as the canonical policy index.
Canonical/JSON-LD injection is likely site-template-level, not authored per page — coordinate with the docs platform to emit `dateModified` from existing frontmatter.
The CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full metadata read; head metadata could not be verified here.
